figure_candidates.label: Figure 5
figure_candidates.caption:
Figure 5. Heterologous reconstitution of moniliphenone (11) and
blennolide C (9) in ScRC01. (A) Biosynthetic pathway of 11 and 9.
(B) Heterologous reconstitution of 11 from chrysophanol (10). (C)
Heterologous reconstitution of 9 from 10. Compounds 11, 9/9′, and
9-RD are fully characterized by NMR and high-resolution MS. The
stereochemistry of C5 is assigned based on the reported stereo-
chemistry of the same carbon in 1.5 The C10 substituent in 9/9′ can
readily epimerize under physiological conditions (Figure S4). 9-RD is
isolated as a single diastereoisomer, but the absolute stereochemistry
at C10 is not determined.

figure_candidates.label: Figure 6
figure_candidates.caption:
Figure 6. First committed step of parnafungin biosynthesis is an unusual biaryl cross-coupling reaction involving a three-enzyme cascade. (A)
Proposed formal biaryl coupling of 9 and anthranilate mediated by ParJ, ParO, and ParD. Compounds 12, 12′, 12-RD, and 12-B are fully
characterized by NMR and HRMS. The stereochemistry of C15 is assigned based on the reported stereochemistry of the same carbon in 1.5 12-RD
and 12-B are isolated as single diastereoisomers, but the absolute stereochemistry at C15a is not determined. (B) Heterologous expression of
ParEGIOJD in ScRC01 with 11 and anthranilate feeding. (C) In vitro activity of ParJ. ParJ (10 μM) was incubated with anthranilate (1 mM), ATP,
coenzyme A (CoA), and MgCl2 (2 mM of each) for 1 h at 25 °C and pH 7.4. A control reaction was performed under the same conditions in the
absence of ParJ. (D) Heterologous expression of ParEGIOD in ScRC01 with 11 and AA-SNAC (as a substitute for AA-CoA) feeding.

figure_candidates.label: Figure 7
figure_candidates.caption:
Figure 7. Reductive amination completes construction of ring-D in 1. (A) Purposed reductive amination catalyzed by ParP and ParT. The more
prominent diastereomers at C15a of compounds 5, 6, and 15 are fully characterized by NMR and HRMS. Structure of compound 15-B is proposed
based on HRMS, UV−vis, and their biosynthetic relationship with 15. The stereochemistry of C5 is assigned based on the reported stereochemistry
of the same carbon in 1.5 The stereochemistry of C15a in all compounds is not determined. (B) Heterologous reconstitution of ParEGIOJDP in
ScRC01 with 11 and anthranilate feeding. ParEGIOJD converts 11 and anthranilate to 12, which is subsequently oxidatively cyclized by ParP to
generate 5. Peaks of 5′ and 6′ are assigned by HRMS, UV−vis, and its biosynthetic relationship with 5 and 6. (C) In vitro enzymatic assay of ParT.
Compound 5 (500 μM) was incubated with NADPH (3 mM) and ParT (10 μM) for 10 min at pH 7.4 and 25 °C. A control reaction was
performed under the same conditions in the absence of ParT.

figure_candidates.label: Figure 8
figure_candidates.caption:
Figure 8. Biosynthesis of 5ILD in parnafungin A (1). (A) Proposed 5ILD formation catalyzed by ParB and ParF. The more prominent
diastereomers at C15a of compounds 1, 2, and 17 are fully characterized by NMR and HRMS. The stereochemistry of C5 is assigned based on the
reported stereochemistry of the same carbon in 1.5 The stereochemistry of C15a in all compounds is not determined. (B) Heterologous
reconstitution of 1 upon coexpression of ParEGI/OJD/PT/BF in ScRC01 with 11 and anthranilate feeding. ParEGI/OJD/PT convert 11 and
anthranilate to 15, which is subsequently converted to 1 and 2 by ParB and ParF. Omitting either one of these two enzymes from the expression
system or mutating the proposed catalytic nucleophile C138 of ParF completely abolished production of 1 and 2. (C) In vitro enzymatic assay of
ParT, ParB, and ParF. Compound 5 (500 μM) was incubated with NADPH (3 mM), ParT (10 μM), ParB (10 μM), and ParF (10 μM) for 30 min
at pH 7.4 and 25 °C. The production of 1 and 2 from the reaction shows that all enzymes are active under in vitro conditions. In the absence of
ParF, the coupled in vitro reaction of ParT and ParB produced a new product, 17, which is the overoxidation shunt product of the proposed on-
pathway intermediate 16.

figure_candidates.label: Figure 9
figure_candidates.caption:
Figure 9. Heterologous reconstitution of parnafungin C (3) and parnafungin D (4). (A) The proposed biosynthetic pathways of 3 and 4. The more
prominent diastereomers at C15a of compounds 3, 4, and 8 are fully characterized by NMR and HRMS. Compound 7 could not be obtained in
sufficient quantity for NMR characterization, but its HRMS, UV−vis spectrum (Figure S7), and biosynthetic relationship with 3 support its
structural assignment. The stereochemistry of C5 is assigned based on the reported stereochemistry of the same carbon in 1.5 The stereochemistry
of C15a in all compounds is not determined. (B) Heterologous reconstitution of 3 upon coexpression of ParTBF and ParX in ScRC01 with 5.
ParTBF converts 5 to 1, which is subsequently converted to 3 by ParX. (C) Heterologous reconstitution of 4 upon coexpression of ParTBF, ParX,
and ParU in ScRC01 with 5. ParTBF converts 5 to 1, which is subsequently converted to 4 by ParX and ParU.
